title: Base plate
description: Raster drawing (PNG), third-angle, scale 1:2: plate with corner radii, four holes and a central bore.

title: Pipe flange
description: Vector PDF, third-angle, scale 1:2: hub flange with a bolt circle of 8 holes.

title: L bracket (one size missing)
description: Raster drawing, third-angle, 1:1. The wall thickness is not dimensioned: it has to be measured on the sheet.

title: Pump skid (DXF assembly)
description: DXF in model space 1:1 with dimension entities: base frame, motor, pump and coupling as an assembly.

title: Vertical vessel (description)
description: Text only: a vertical tank with ellipsoidal heads, four legs and two nozzles.
text: Vertical storage tank. Cylindrical shell 800 mm outside diameter and 1500 mm straight height, with 2:1 semi-ellipsoidal heads at the top and bottom. It stands on four legs of 100 x 100 mm square section, equally spaced at 45 degrees, reaching 400 mm below the bottom of the lower head. One 100A nozzle (OD 114.3 mm) on the centre of the top head, 150 mm high. One 50A side nozzle (OD 60.5 mm) 300 mm above the bottom tangent line, pointing along +X and ending 600 mm from the vessel axis.

title: Stepped shaft (description)
description: Text only: a turned shaft with four diameters, chamfers and a keyway.
text: Stepped shaft along the X axis, starting at x = 0: diameter 40 mm for 60 mm, then diameter 50 mm for 150 mm, then diameter 45 mm for 40 mm, then diameter 35 mm for 70 mm. 1 mm chamfers on both end faces. A keyway 10 mm wide, 5 mm deep and 50 mm long, centred on the 50 mm section, on top (+Z).

title: Tubular tower with tank (description)
description: Text only: a tower made only of pipes, with a deck plate and a tank - for the beam and shell analysis model (Export tab).
text: Tower of steel pipes. Four vertical legs, pipe OD 273 mm x 9.3 mm wall, at the corners of a 4000 mm square, from z = 0 to z = 9000 mm. Horizontal braces, pipe OD 168.3 x 7.1 mm, between the legs at z = 3000, 6000 and 9000 mm. X-braces, pipe OD 114.3 x 6 mm, in every face and every bay. A 12 mm deck plate, 4400 x 4400 mm, centred on the top of the legs. On the deck, at its centre, a vertical tank 2000 mm in diameter, 2500 mm straight height, 2:1 ellipsoidal heads, 10 mm wall.

title: Turbine and generator unit, 1925 (hard)
description: Real drawing, HAER AL-47-A (Wilson Dam): half section of a 35,000 hp Francis turbine and generator. No dimensions at all - sizes only from the graphic scale bars; two scales on one sheet.
text: Model the turbine and generator unit as a layout model: generator, exciter, shaft, Francis runner, wicket gates and stay vanes, spiral distributor, draft tube and the surrounding concrete.
source: Historic American Engineering Record (HAER), National Park Service; Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain (no known restrictions), via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Steel deck truss, erection plan (hard)
description: Real drawing, HAER FL-12 (Apalachicola River Bridge): photograph of a 1934 erection plan - two Warren trusses, top and bottom laterals, sway frames; feet-and-inch dimensions, member marks.
source: Historic American Engineering Record (HAER), National Park Service; Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain (no known restrictions), via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Turbine building, three sheets (hard)
description: Real drawing set, HAER CT-185-C (Haddam Neck plant): turbine support outline, machine location sections and the operating floor plan; 21,600 x 13,000 px scans, feet-and-inch dimensions.
text: Layout model of the turbine-generator support (pedestal), the machines on it and the operating floor.
source: Historic American Engineering Record (HAER), National Park Service; Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain (no known restrictions), via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Ship engine room, plan and section (hard)
description: Real drawing set, HAER CA-337 (tanker Mission Santa Ynez): plan and longitudinal section of the aft engine and pump rooms - about forty machines on two levels and the shaft line; the plan is drawn with the frames running the other way than in the section. Graphic scale in feet and metres.
text: Layout model of the engine room and pump room machinery: main propulsion motor and shaft line, main condenser, boiler, turbo-generators, main cargo pumps, the larger auxiliary pumps and tanks, and the flats they stand on.
source: Historic American Engineering Record (HAER), National Park Service; Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division. Public domain (no known restrictions), via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Pumping engine, book illustration (hard)
description: Real drawing, Holly high-duty pumping engine (New Catechism of the Steam Engine, 1904): one sectional elevation without dimensions or scale; the flywheel runs off the top of the picture. One size is given in words, everything else follows from the proportions.
text: Layout model of the pumping engine: steam cylinders, frame and crank, flywheel, pump cylinders, air vessel and the masonry foundation. The foundation is 12 m long; take every other size from the proportions of the drawing. The engine is about as deep as the flywheel diameter.
source: Hawkins, New Catechism of the Steam Engine (1904). Public domain (published before 1929), via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Inverted V-16 engine, five sheets (hard)
description: Patent drawings US 2,468,976 (1949): side elevation, transverse and longitudinal sections and plan views of a liquid-cooled inverted V-16 aircraft engine on five sheets - crankcase, cylinder banks, crankshaft, heads, manifolds. No dimensions and no scale; one size is given in words.
text: Layout model of the engine: crankcase, the two inverted cylinder banks of eight cylinders with their heads and camshaft covers, crankshaft, oil sump, intake and exhaust manifolds, reduction gear housing at the front and accessory housing at the rear. The crankcase is about 2900 mm long (assumed - the drawings carry no scale); take every other size from the proportions.
source: US patent 2,468,976 (A. G. Herreshoff et al., 1949), published without a copyright notice - public domain in the United States.

title: Automatic transmission, three sheets (hard)
description: Patent drawings US 2,193,304 (1940, the first mass-produced automatic transmission): vertical section of the whole gearbox with planetary gear sets, clutches and brake bands, cross sections of the gear trains and the control unit on three sheets. No dimensions and no scale.
text: Layout model of the transmission: case and bell housing, input and output shafts, the planetary gear sets with their drums, clutch packs and brake bands, the oil pump and the valve body. The case is about 750 mm long (assumed - the drawings carry no scale); take every other size from the proportions.
source: US patent 2,193,304 (E. A. Thompson, 1940), published without a copyright notice - public domain in the United States.

title: Fan-cooled induction motor (hard)
description: Patent drawing US 2,449,502 (1948): longitudinal and transverse sections of a totally enclosed fan-cooled squirrel-cage motor - frame with cooling ribs, stator core and windings, rotor, shaft, end shields with bearings, fan and fan cover. No dimensions and no scale.
text: Layout model of the motor: frame with cooling ribs and feet, stator core with end windings, rotor core with end rings, shaft, both end shields with bearings, external fan and fan cover. The frame is about 420 mm in outside diameter (assumed - the drawing carries no scale); take every other size from the proportions.
source: US patent 2,449,502 (J. H. Penney, 1948), published without a copyright notice - public domain in the United States.
